_readme: Per-issue ENGINEERING spec: the numbers that make a prompt well-specified.
tools/prompts_chatgpt.py joins this with issues_chatgpt.json (art direction: register,
subject, geometry, text) and issues/table.json (title, arc, beat).
Why a second file: issues_chatgpt.json says WHAT the image is. This file says HOW
BIG and WHERE, in numbers the generator can check. Splitting them keeps the art
direction readable as prose and the geometry auditable as arithmetic.
bbox    : [cx, cy, w, h] as fractions of frame width/height. cx/cy is the CENTRE
of the subject's bounding box, not its origin. w/h are the box size.
math    : list of measured statements. Every number here is checkable by eye on
the finished image. These are what separate an engineered prompt from
an adjective. Order them as a reader would verify them.
detail  : material and light notes specific to this subject, not the register.
neg     : extra negatives beyond the shared ones. Issue-specific only.
palette : optional override of the register palette, as [[name, hex, share]].
value   : optional override of the tonal split [shadow, mid, light, specular].

math: Rings: exactly 11 concentric rings. Outer radius of ring k = 0.420 * 0.78^k of frame width, so the radii fall 42.0%, 32.8%, 25.5%, 19.9%, 15.6%, 12.1%, 9.5%, 7.4%, 5.7%, 4.5%, 3.5% of frame width — a 12.0:1 fall from outermost to innermost.
Centres drift 0.006 of frame width east per step, so the stack leans 0.06 east over its depth and the recession never reads as a flat bullseye.
Vanishing point at (50%, 86%) — low, so the eye falls DOWN and inward, never up.
The road is a band 0.055 of frame width entering the left edge at y=44% and leaving the right edge at y=44%. Slope exactly 0. It is horizontal in the frame; it is the RINGS that spiral, not the road.
detail: Ring material: cut stone, quarried — each ring shows tool-chatter along its inner wall and a chipped lip on the outer edge, all following the ring's own curvature.
Light enters from the upper left at 40 degrees: ring outer walls lit, inner walls in shadow, so each ring reads as a solid with depth rather than a drawn circle.
The ground is not flat black — it carries the same engraved line-work as the rings at 40% of their frequency, so the subject never floats on a void.
neg: no sky, no horizon line, no ground plane — the frame is rings only
no birds, no stars, no moon

math: Figure area = 0.085 x 0.16 = 1.36% of the frame. It must stay under a tenth of the frame; if it grows, the whole image loses its scale.
Stair: 11 treads, rise 0.062 of frame height per tread, run 0.078 of frame width. Pitch = atan(0.062/0.078) = 38.5 degrees, raking up and to the RIGHT.
Figure stands on the 3rd tread from the bottom, at (34%, 74%).
Stair vanishing point at (86%, 18%) — off-frame up-right, so the stair turns AWAY from the viewer rather than coming at them.
The last 2 treads are cut off by the right edge: the stair leaves the frame, which is what makes it turn.
detail: Figure is a silhouette in the register's cold ink only, hood up, no face, no hands — the pose carries it.
Stair is drawn in line-work that thins with distance: full weight at the bottom tread, 30% weight at tread 8, hairline at tread 11.
The whole stair casts one soft shadow down-left, confirming a single light source at upper right.
neg: no face, no eyes, no hands — strictly from behind
no second figure
no railing or balustrade

math: Four doorways, one inside the next. Opening width of arch k = 0.580 * 0.62^k of frame width: 58.0%, 36.0%, 22.3%, 13.8% — each one 62% of the one outside it.
Opening height follows the same ratio: 0.660 * 0.62^k = 66.0%, 40.9%, 25.4%, 15.7% of frame height.
Centre of arch k drifts 0.020 of frame width east per step: 50%, 52%, 54%, 56%. The tunnel is therefore NOT concentric — it leans, which is what makes it ruinous rather than schematic.
Depth cue is tonal, not linear: each successive arch is 22% darker than the one in front of it, so four arches occupy four distinct value bands.
detail: Each arch is broken differently: arch 1 intact at the crown, arch 2 missing its upper-left voussoir, arch 3 collapsed to a springer on the right, arch 4 a fragment of jamb only.
The stone between arches is coursed masonry, courses running level, so the arches are cut INTO the wall rather than built from it.
Grit and fallen blocks collect at the base of each arch, thinning inward — debris also obeys the 0.62 ratio.
neg: no figure anywhere — this image has no one in it
no light source visible
no readable inscription on the stone

math: The opening is built from TWO arcs of UNEQUAL radius: left arc radius 0.310 of frame width centred at (36.5%, 55%); right arc radius 0.240 centred at (64.5%, 55%). A 1.29:1 radius ratio.
The two arcs intersect twice, 0.36 of frame width apart, and the opening is the lens between them: 0.18 wide at its widest, apex 0.44 of frame height above the spring line.
The opening's own axis is tilted 11 degrees off vertical, apex at (50%, 42%).
No mirror line exists anywhere in the frame: for every element at (x, y) there is no matching element at (1-x, y), and the minimum left-right asymmetry is 0.04 of frame width.
detail: The frame is heavy cut stone: 0.08 of frame width thick, with a chamfered inner reveal that catches light on one side and drops to black on the other.
Inside the opening: pure void, no depth, no second room, no glow. The opening is the absence, not a window.
Beyond the frame the wall is coursed and weathered; within it the stone is dressed and precise. That contrast is the whole image.
neg: no handle, no hinge, no door leaf
no light inside the opening
no symmetry of any kind

math: Mirror axis at exactly x = 50.0%. Reflecting anything left of it gives its twin right of it, congruent to within 0 — a perfect bilateral mirror, no tolerance.
The chair's seat spans 0.21 of frame width either side of the axis; total silhouette 0.42 wide by 0.44 high, centred at (50%, 55%).
Seam width 0: the transition at the axis is a hard cut with no gradient band of any width.
Three details are deliberately seeded out of register — two on the left, one on the right — so the reflection does not fully close and the object stops being an object.
detail: An ordinary wooden chair: four legs, seat, slatted back, nothing special about it. Its plainness is the point.
Wood grain follows the real construction: vertical on the legs, horizontal on the seat rails.
Cast shadow beneath it, mirrored too, so the shadow confirms the geometry rather than explaining it.
neg: no ornament on the chair
no second chair
no human figure
no gradient across the seam

math: Figure occupies 0.05 x 0.09 = 0.45% of the frame — the smallest subject in the series. It must not be enlarged for legibility; its smallness is the image.
Tower occupies the full frame width at the top and runs from y=0% down to y=80%: 0.80 of frame height against the figure's 0.09 — a scale ratio of 8.9:1.
The figure is placed at 32% across, 90% down — low, off-centre, corner-weighted — and reaches up and slightly right.
Detail budget: the figure is a clean silhouette with no interior detail at all. 100% of the rendered detail budget goes to the tower.
detail: Tower is masonry: courses, corbelled stages, a narrowing profile, and a top that exits the frame so its height is unknowable.
Light rakes the tower from the upper right, catching every course edge; the figure is entirely in the tower's shadow.
The tower's face has depth in shadow — recesses, a narrow window slit, nothing lit.
neg: no face on the figure, no gesture detail
no second figure
no sky detail, no clouds
no ground, no horizon

math: Two storks, seam at exactly x = 50.0%, hard edge, 0 gradient.
Each stork 0.28 wide by 0.62 high, centres at (34%, 52%) and (66%, 52%) — 0.32 of frame width separates their centres, so their beaks cross the axis and overlap by 0.06.
Beak tips converge to points 0.16 apart: (42%, 44%) and (58%, 44%). They aim at each other and do not touch.
Ink-area split is 62% cold / 38% hot. The cold side is heavier, so the pair reads as arguing rather than balanced.
detail: Long legs, long neck, heavy dagger beak — drawn as line-work with the neck's curve doubled on the inside to show tension.
Cold side: cyan line-work, low value, the body mostly in shadow. Hot side: magenta and ember, high value, rim-lit along the back.
Feather detail is three strokes per body, not more; the birds must read as two shapes arguing, not as two illustrations.
neg: no wings spread into display — the beaks do the talking
no ground line
no mirror gradient

math: Split axis at exactly x = 50.0%. Left half 0.46 of frame width, right half 0.46, seam 0 wide, hard cut, no gradient and no blend zone.
Form: 0.86 wide by 0.70 high, centred at (50%, 48%), bilaterally symmetric to within 0 — this is the series' signature look and it is exact, not approximate.
Colour temperature divides 1:1 by area. Every square millimetre left of the axis is cold; every one right of it is hot. No shared ink.
Folds: 9 convolutions per hemisphere, mirrored, so the whole form reads as one brain-like structure and not as two unrelated shapes.
Interior structure: 3 nested chambers per side, mirrored, opening toward the seam.
detail: Ornate and organic at once: the outline is engraved line-work, the chambers are engraved line-work, and the whole thing has the density of a tattoo flash rather than a diagram.
Cold side glows from inside: cyan light source within the chambers, no external key.
Hot side burns from outside: ember light on the outer convolutions, magenta in the recesses.
The seam is the brightest line in the image — a hairline of both temperatures meeting, never crossing.
neg: no neural-network node diagram, no circles-and-lines
no text, no labels
no third colour anywhere

math: Exactly 640 component keys in a brick lattice of 40 columns by 16 rows. Each component is 0.0155 of frame width wide and 0.0188 of frame height tall, laid with a half-key offset on alternate rows.
At 200 px the frame is 200 px wide, so each component is 3.1 px wide — below the threshold where a key reads as a key. The macro form is readable only at full size and dissolves on approach.
Macro silhouette is unmistakably a key: bow 0.18 of frame height at the left, shank 0.44 long, ward teeth 0.09 deep at the right.
Every component is identical: same angle, same length, same bow. No two differ by more than 0.002 of frame width.
detail: Each component key is itself a real key — bow, shank, bit, ward — drawn in miniature line-work at a density of about 6 strokes each.
Machined finish: every component catches the same single light at the same angle, so the macro form gains a metallic gradient from uniformity alone.
Cast shadow of the whole assembly falls down-right; the shadows of the components fall down-left, which is what makes the mass read as built from parts.
neg: no component may be unique or hand-varied
no gears, no cogs, no springs
no text or stamped markings

math: Panel grid: 3 columns by 2 rows. Outer margin 0.055 of frame width; gutters 0.035 between panels and to the frame edge.
Panel size = ((1 - 2*0.055) - 2*0.035) / 3 = 0.2733 wide, and ((1 - 2*0.055) - 0.035) / 2 = 0.4275 high. Every panel is exactly that size; the grid is not eyeballed.
Panel flow: row 1 left to right, then row 2 left to right. The figure walks EAST — left to right — through all six panels, so the reading direction and the travel direction agree.
Figure occupies 0.18 wide by 0.30 high inside each panel, at the same relative height in all six so the eye tracks one continuous walk.
Lettering: 3 rows per panel, each glyph 0.03 of frame height, baseline-aligned to a 0.045 grid. Shapes only — none of them spells anything.
detail: Confident brush line with real tapering: strokes are thick on the shadow side, thin on the light, and the line thins on the far figure.
Screentone at 40% dot density for shadow, 20% for the second plane, solid black for the darkest — three tones, no gradients.
The paper is cream and slightly warm; the ink is true black with no brown in it.
neg: no word may be readable in any panel
no speech balloon, no caption box
no accent colour — this page is black on cream only

math: 24 vertebrae. Centres follow an Archimedean spiral: r(θ) = 0.060 + 0.011 * θ where θ is in degrees, stepping 15 degrees per vertebra, k = 0..23.
Total turn 345 degrees, so the column wraps just under one full revolution. Radius grows 0.060 -> 0.415 of frame width — a 6.9:1 expansion from base to tip.
Each vertebra is 0.11 of frame width wide by 0.055 high, and each overlaps its neighbour by 0.02 so the column reads as articulated rather than stacked.
Rise is 0.024 of frame height per step, 23 steps: the column climbs 0.552 of frame height while it spirals outward.
detail: Vertebrae are machined, not anatomical: each is a symmetric disc with a central bore and a chamfered rim, identical from the base to the tip except in size.
Lit from within: each bore is the light source, so the glow is centred in each body and falls to zero 0.028 of frame width from the bore centre.
Between vertebrae the background drops to near-black, so the light reads as discontinuous — a chain of lamps, not a glowing rope.
neg: no skull, no ribcage, no human anatomy
no spinal cord or soft tissue
no text

math: Eight figures on a circle of radius 0.30 of frame width, centred at (50%, 50%), spaced 45 degrees apart, first figure at 22.5 degrees so that NO figure sits on the vertical or horizontal axis.
Each figure 0.13 of frame width by 0.30 of frame height, standing, feet at radius 0.30, heads at radius 0.30 - 0.30.
Perfect radial repetition: the eight are congruent to within 0 — no variation in pose, height, angle, or colour.
Each figure is a closed shape with exactly ONE piece cut out of it: an aperture 0.035 wide by 0.055 high, positioned at the figure's own centre, in all eight.
detail: Each closed shape is a glyph, not a body: a solid silhouette with flat shoulders and no head, drawn in one ink with no modelling.
The cut-out is the same colour as the ground, so it reads as light coming through rather than paint removed.
A single flat colour across all eight. No shading inside any figure; separation is by outline weight alone.
neg: no faces on any of the eight
no variation between the eight
no connecting line, no circle drawn between them

math: Exactly three wings, spaced 120 degrees apart, all rooted at a common centre with root radius 0.10 of frame width at (50%, 50%).
Each wing is 0.30 of frame width long with a chord of 0.11 — a 2.7:1 aspect — and tapers to a point.
Extension is one-twentieth PAST full: 0.95 of the maximum stroke length, missing 5%. It is caught, not at full extension and not folded.
Wing beat angle: the tip of each wing sits 0.14 of frame width from the root, so all three tips fall on the same circle of radius 0.24.
detail: The glyph-form is a single closed body with three wings cut from it; the wings are the same ink as the body, separated by outline only.
The wing membrane carries 5 vein strokes per wing, angled back toward the root — structure, not decoration.
A faint impression in the ink behind the beat, as though the air moved: this is the only soft mark in the image.
neg: exactly three wings — not four, not two
no bird, no insect, no anatomical wing
no motion blur across the wings

math: Hub: radius 0.07 at (50%, 50%). Eight spokes run out to eight nodes on radius 0.30; node radius 0.035.

Outer ring at radius 0.42 carries 120 labels at a pitch of 2*pi*0.42/120 = 0.0220 of frame width, while each label is 0.030 wide. Labels therefore overlap their neighbours by 27% and the ring breaks into noise.
Label budget: 8 node labels plus 120 outer labels plus 18 axis captions = 146 text-shaped marks in the frame.
This is the one image in the series that is DELIBERATELY unreadable at thumbnail size. Its density is the warning, not its style.
detail: Node faces carry simple icons; the outer ring carries labels that collide; the axis captions sit at three angles.
Everything is hairline and aligned to a 0.01 grid. Nothing is hand-drawn wobble; the chaos is entirely in the density.
A faint vignette pulls the corners down so the centre still reads, even though nothing else does.
neg: no label may be a real word
do NOT tidy this up — the over-density is the subject
no colour beyond the register palette

math: The beam runs corner to corner: enters at (2%, 96%) and exits at (98%, 6%). Its angle above horizontal = atan(0.90/0.96) = 43.2 degrees.
The beam is a cone, not a line: 0.10 of frame width at the source corner widening to 0.26 at the far corner — a 2.6:1 spread.
It strikes the glyph-form at exactly (50%, 50%), which is both the frame centre and the beam's midpoint.
Glyph-form 0.24 wide by 0.52 high, standing, centred on the strike point. It is the ONLY object in the frame the beam touches.
detail: The light is pale wine-red, volumetric: it scatters, so its edges are soft while its core is dense. It is the only soft-edged element in an otherwise hard-edged image.
The glyph stands in the beam's path and is lit from the beam's direction, so its own shadow falls away from the viewer and is barely visible.
The ground outside the beam is near-black but not empty — engraved line-work at 30% frequency, so it holds tone without competing.
neg: no second light source
no lens flare, no starburst
no other object in the beam

math: Two robed figures, each 0.26 of frame width by 0.44 of frame height, centres at (34%, 58%) and (66%, 58%).
Both tilt inward 17 degrees toward a single point between them at (50%, 60%) — the axis of each body points at that one point and nowhere else.
Contact: one hand rests on the other's chest. The contact patch is 0.05 wide by 0.06 high, and it is the ONLY place the two silhouettes touch.
The point at (50%, 60%) is where the two 17-degree axes cross. Nothing else in the frame shares that coordinate.
detail: Robe folds fall vertically from the shoulders and gather at the contact point, so the drapery itself points at what matters.
Monochrome, near-photographic modelling: 7 value steps across each robe, and the two robes are lit from opposite sides so their shared edge is the brightest line in the image.
Gold construction overlays the pair — one thin circle through both heads, one rule along the 17-degree axis.
neg: no faces — both heads are bowed and closed
no third figure
no background incident, no floor line

math: The holder: 0.11 wide by 0.20 high at (38%, 66%). The glyph-form it holds: 0.26 wide by 0.34 high at (56%, 52%). They are different sizes; the figure is calm and the thing it holds is the subject.
Decay: exactly 22 fragments shed from the glyph's outer band, defined as everything more than 0.06 of the glyph's width from its outline.
Fragment sizes run 0.010 to 0.045 of frame width. Fragment count falls with distance from the glyph: 9 in the first 0.06 of travel, 7 in the next, 6 in the last.
The glyph's CORE — everything inside that 0.06 band — is fully intact and fully solid. Decay starts only at the edges.
detail: The fragments are pieces OF the glyph — the same ink, the same line-work, the same shapes it was made of — not new objects.
They rotate as they travel, each one at a different angle, so the loss reads as disintegration rather than as a spray.
The figure's hands and posture are steady and closed. Nothing about the figure suggests panic; the danger is entirely in what it holds.
neg: the decay must not look like fire, smoke, or sparks
no explosion
no second figure
no face on the holder

math: One eye-form: 0.62 of frame width by 0.44 of frame height, centred at (50%, 50%). Exactly four pupils.
Pupils sit on a 2x2 lattice, spacing 0.19 wide by 0.15 high, pupil radius 0.075 — centres at (40.5%, 42.5%), (59.5%, 42.5%), (40.5%, 57.5%), (59.5%, 57.5%).
Each pupil shows a different horizontal band of the SAME scene: the four bands are y = 30-36%, 36-42%, 48-54% and 60-66% of frame height, so they are stacked, level, and never overlapping.
The pupil circles touch the iris rim at exactly one point each, tangent, not intersecting.
detail: The iris and sclera are drawn in line-work, hard-edged, no wet highlight — this is an engraved eye, not a photographic one.
Inside each pupil the band is a compressed strip of the same engraved world, one colour temperature per band: cyan, pale blue, magenta, ember.
The lash line is the heaviest stroke in the image and the only place the line-work doubles.
neg: exactly four pupils
no eyelashes beyond the one lash line
no third colour in the pupils
no face around the eye

math: The void is a standing-person shape: 0.22 of frame width by 0.56 of frame height, centred at (50%, 52%) — head, shoulders, body, no limbs.
Inside the void, absolute luminance 0.00 with NO texture of any kind: no noise, no dots, no gradient, no dust, no grain. Sample it and every pixel reads 0. This is testable and it is the image.
Ring of light: outer radius 0.30, ring thickness 0.045, so the lit band runs from radius 0.255 to 0.300.
Glow beyond the ring falls to zero over a further 0.09 of frame width. Total lit-plus-glow radius 0.39; void-plus-ring-plus-glow occupies 0.48 of the frame area.
detail: The light is cold: cyan at the ring's inner edge moving to pale blue at its outer, and it is the only light in the image.
Everything outside the glow is engraved line-work at low contrast — present enough to hold the frame, never enough to compete.
The void's edge is razor-sharp against the glow, with no feather. A soft edge would read as smoke; a hard edge reads as an absence.
neg: no figure inside the void
no arms, no legs
nothing at all inside the void — not even grain
no warm colour

math: One rose, dead centre at (50%, 48%), 0.24 of frame width by 0.30 of frame height. This is the ONE cover in the series that is dead-centre, and it is deliberate.
Value ladder: 7 discrete steps from 0.02 (deepest petal shadow) to 0.98 (specular on the top petal). No continuous gradient — 7 tones, hard boundaries between them, like a duotone engraving.
Perspective grid: horizon at y = 62%, one-point, 9 verticals converging on (50%, 62%), spaced 0.11 of frame width at the near edge and compressing toward the vanishing point.
Cast shadow falls down-LEFT (away from the register's usual key), offset 0.06 of frame width from the stem. It is soft at 0.02 of frame width.
detail: Petals are individually drawn — 14 outer, 9 inner, each with its own edge and its own value step. The bloom is real, not a texture.
Two thorns on the stem, one leaf, both fully resolved. The plant is a plant, drawn by someone who has drawn plants.
Monochrome warm-grey subject on a near-black ground, with the register's gold frame and gold construction over it.
neg: no vase, no water, no table
no second flower
no dew drops or sparkle effects
no colour in the rose itself

math: Six figures, heights 0.24, 0.34, 0.28, 0.32, 0.26, 0.30 of frame height — deliberately unequal, so the cast has no rhythm.
Body axes at six different angles spanning 62 degrees total: 0, 12, 25, 37, 50, 62 degrees. No two share an angle.
Minimum separation between any two figure centres 0.13 of frame width, so no two figures can be read as a pair or a group.
All six face EAST — all six noses and leading shoulders point in the same direction. The shared direction is what makes six strangers one scene.
detail: Flat vector bodies: solid fills, no outline, no modelling. Every figure is one flat colour and the six colours are drawn from the register palette.
Each is caught mid-action at the same instant, so limbs are extended at incompatible angles and nothing is at rest.
No ground plane. The six float on the engraved ground, which carries line-work at 25% frequency.
neg: no two figures may share a pose or an angle
no ground line, no horizon
no faces — figures are 0.24-0.34 high and faceless

math: Two symbols at equal height, both 0.52 of frame height: caduceus centred at (34%, 50%), double helix at (66%, 50%).
They share ONE base plinth 0.30 of frame width by 0.07 high, its top edge at y = 80%. Neither symbol floats and neither stands alone.
Equal finish: both are drawn with the same stroke weight (0.004 of frame width), the same contour-pass count (9), and the same level of detail. Neither symbol is more resolved than the other.
Horizontal centre-to-centre distance 0.32 of frame width, so they stand side by side rather than overlapping.
detail: Both symbols are drawn in full, in the tradition of engraved scientific plates: consistent line weight, no stylisation, no modern simplification.
The caduceus has 2 wings, 2 snakes crossing 7 times, and a staff; the helix has 2 strands crossing 11 times over 0.52 of frame height.
Both are near-photographic in their modelling — cylindrical shading on the staff, refracted shading where the strands pass.
Gold construction overlays both: one circle through both tops, one baseline along the plinth.
neg: no modern medical iconography, no simplified glyph versions
no text, no labels
no third symbol

math: Filigree field fills 0.86 of frame width, inset from the gold frame by 0.07. The remaining 0.07 is the frame and nothing else.
Three strand pitches — 0.030, 0.055 and 0.090 of frame width — interlace in a 4-fold symmetric weave about (50%, 50%). The three pitches are what make it read as woven rather than as noise.
Symmetry: 4-fold. Reflect or rotate any element about the centre and its twin is present to within 0.
Representational content: exactly zero. No figure, no object, no face, no ground plane, no horizon, no negative-space shape that a viewer could resolve into a thing.
detail: Each strand is an engraved line of constant weight that passes OVER one neighbour and UNDER the next, and the crossings are drawn so the over/under is unambiguous.
Line-work density at the register's high frequency, but every stroke is part of the weave — there is no filler hatching.
Gold on near-black with a warm crimson underlayer at 20% density in the deepest interstices, so the weave has depth without shading.
neg: nothing must be depictable — if a viewer can name what the shape is, it has failed
no central medallion, no boss, no focal point
no empty area larger than 0.09 of frame width

math: Gold double rule, inset 0.045 and 0.062 of frame width from the frame edge. Corner ornaments 0.09 x 0.09 at all four corners.
Cartouche: 0.52 of frame width by 0.34 of frame height, centred at (50%, 50%), with a 0.010 gold rule around it.
The cartouche interior is EMPTY: luminance varies by less than 0.02 across the whole 0.52 x 0.34 field. It is a flat field, not a faded image and not a faint suggestion.
The blank cartouche is the largest single area in the frame at 17.7% of its area, and nothing occupies any of it.
detail: The rule is engraved gold with a real bevel: lit on the upper-left edge, shadowed on the lower-right, so the frame has thickness.
The engraved background continues BEHIND the cartouche at half strength, so the cartouche reads as a plate laid over the page rather than a hole cut in it.
Scattered gold numerals and equations texture the field around the cartouche — meaningless, suggestive, never resolving into a readable word.
neg: the cartouche must be completely empty
no signature, no inscription, no pencil ghost
no name, no number, no monogram anywhere

math: Three concentric dials sharing the centre (50%, 50%): radii 0.10, 0.20 and 0.30 of frame width. A 3:1 ratio between outer and inner.
Needle: 0.28 of frame width long, 0.006 wide, resting at 41 degrees from vertical, pivoting on the exact centre.
Outer scale: 60 major ticks at 6-degree pitch, each 0.018 of frame width long; 300 minor ticks at 1.2-degree pitch, each 0.008 long. 360 ticks total.
Ticks only. Zero glyphs — not numeral-shaped, not letter-shaped, not even decorative. Every mark on every scale is a stroke of constant width.
detail: The instrument is built like real equipment: bevelled dial rims with a highlight arc on the upper left, recessed faces, a shadow under each rim lip.
Each dial face is a flat tint with the register's faint grid showing through at 15% — the grid is part of the object, not a background.
The needle is the only element that casts a shadow, and it falls down-right across the outer dial.
neg: no numbers, no letters, no digits anywhere on any dial
no brand name, no model number
no more than three dials

math: Eight nodes on a circle of radius 0.28 of frame width centred at (50%, 48%), spaced 45 degrees apart, first at 0 degrees.
Node radius 0.055. Spokes 0.005 of frame width wide running from the core rim to each node centre.
Core: radius 0.09 at the exact centre, and it is EMPTY — nothing inside it, no icon, no label, no fill.
Node faces are BLANK: zero marks on all eight. The layout is the deliverable; the labels are the typesetter's job.
detail: Each node is a circle outlined in one bright colour with a 2px-equivalent rim and a completely clear interior.
Faint concentric rings behind the node ring at radius 0.20 and 0.36, at 20% contrast — depth, not structure.
Corner tick marks at the frame edge and a faint vignette, so the diagram sits on a ground rather than floating.
neg: every node face must be blank
the core must be empty
no caption block, no title, no year

math: Nine cells, 3x3. Outer margin 0.030 of frame width, gutters 0.020. Cell size = ((1 - 0.060) - 2*0.020)/3 = 0.2900 wide, and 0.2900 high. The grid is arithmetically even.
Outline weight 0.014 of frame width, and it VARIES by up to 35% from cell to cell (0.009 to 0.019). Constant weight would read as precise; varying weight reads as badly hand-made.
Fill: flat mustard at 100%, no gradient, no highlight, no shadow. Fill covers 100% of each cell interior.
Structural correctness: 3 rows, 4 connector stubs, 2 return paths, all in the right places. The structure is right; the execution is not.
detail: Square corners everywhere — no rounding, no bevelling, no gradients, nothing that a competent draughtsman would add.
The mustard is slightly dirty, as if mixed by hand and not quite consistent between cells.
This is the one image in the series that is deliberately BAD. Do not improve it. Ugly and structurally correct is the entire argument.
neg: do NOT make this look good — clumsy execution is the subject
no gradients, no shadows, no rounded corners, no bevels
no colour other than mustard, the outline ink, and the ground

math: Four badge callouts, each 0.20 of frame width by 0.08 of frame height, in the frame's corners: (18%, 18%), (82%, 18%), (18%, 82%), (82%, 82%).
Four leader lines, 0.004 of frame width wide, running from each badge to an empty box 0.10 wide by 0.07 high at (38%, 34%), (62%, 34%), (38%, 66%), (62%, 66%).
Every leader line terminates ON an empty box. No line ends on a part, and every box it ends on has nothing in it.
Badge interiors are uniform: zero marks, zero text, zero glyphs. All four are equally empty.
detail: The assembly beneath is real: two mating plates, four bolt bosses, a gasket line — drawn properly, in the register's line-work.
Badges are drawn as real badges: rounded rectangles with a hairline border and a drop shadow, which makes their emptiness conspicuous.
The empty boxes are white and flat — brighter than anything else in the frame, so the eye goes to the failure.
neg: no badge may contain text
no leader line may terminate on a part
no part may be labelled anywhere

math: One polyhedron, 0.34 of frame width across, centred at (50%, 50%). Eight wheels on a circle of radius 0.30, spaced 45 degrees apart, first at 22.5 degrees.
Wheel radius 0.065. Each wheel is a circle in outline with 8 spokes, drawn in line-work and nothing else.
Polyhedron has ZERO flat fill: it is pure line-work, all edges visible, no hidden-line removal.
Nothing else in the frame: no key, no legend, no title block, no dimension arrows, no callouts. 1 object, 0 annotations. This is the reusable version and it stays reusable.
detail: Pure line-work on the dark ground: every line the same weight, no fill, no shading, no colour variation.
The polyhedron's edges are drawn as construction lines extending 0.02 past the vertices, which is what makes it read as a drawing rather than an object.
The wheels are drawn as circles in perspective — ellipses — so the ring reads as a ring and not as a flat halo.
neg: no key, no legend, no title block, no caption
no dimension lines or arrows
no fill on the polyhedron

math: The word AMPHETAMEMES: 12 characters, all caps, cap height 0.085 of frame height.

Letter width 0.0562 of frame width — 0.66 of the cap height, the ratio of a roman capital — with tracking +0.008 between letters. Total word width = 12*0.0562 + 11*0.008 = 0.674 + 0.088 = 0.762 of frame width — check it spans 76% and no more.
Centred horizontally: first letter starts at x = 11.9%, last ends at x = 88.1%. Baseline at y = 54.5%, cap line at y = 46.0%.
This is the ONLY text in the image. Total text-shaped marks in the frame: 12. Zero others — not in the border, not in the corners, not in the background numerals.
detail: Engraved roman capitals with real stroke modulation: stems 0.008 wide, horizontals 0.006, serifs bracketed. Letterforms are cut, not typeset.
The word sits in the cartouche's centre, on the same axis as the gold frame, so the frame and the word share one centre.
The engraved background numerals and equations continue around the word but must not crowd it — a clear band of 0.04 of frame height above the cap line and below the baseline.
neg: AMPHETAMEMES is the only text — no subtitle, no issue number, no date, no publisher mark
no letters behind the word
no misspelling: spell it A-M-P-H-E-T-A-M-E-M-E-S

math: Eight swatches in a column at x = 14-21%, each 0.07 of frame width by 0.05 high, on a vertical pitch of 0.075. Column top at y = 18%, so swatch i's centre sits at y = 20.5% + i*7.5%.
Eight index numerals 1 to 8 at cap height 0.030 of frame height, at x = 24%, baseline-aligned to each swatch's centre.
The eight-node ring sits on the right: centre (66%, 50%), radius 0.26, nodes at 45-degree intervals, node i at angle i*45 degrees.
Swatch i, numeral i and node i all sit on one shared 0.075 vertical pitch. Misregistration greater than 0.004 of frame height breaks the rule — align them exactly.
detail: Swatches are flat fills with a hairline border, drawn to print-legibility: each colour is a real pigment value, not a screen.
The ring on the right uses the same eight colours as its node outlines, so the key genuinely keys the diagram.
Leader lines from each numeral to its node are 0.0025 of frame width — the thinnest line in the frame, and still straight.
neg: the only text is the numerals 1 to 8
no word, no header, no title, no caption anywhere on the sheet
no swatch may be out of order with its node

math: Filigree field 0.82 of frame width, 4-fold symmetric about (50%, 50%), strands at two pitches only — 0.035 and 0.070 — so the weave is simpler than issue 23's and therefore more graceful.

One region, 0.14 wide by 0.11 high, in the lower-left quadrant at (36%, 66%), resolves just far enough to suggest a standing figure — and then stops. Shoulder and hood edge, no face, no limbs, no object held.
That region is the ONLY quasi-representational area in the frame. The other 0.82 x 0.82 minus 0.0154 of it carries no suggestible shape at all.
Density inside that region: 0.34 of its area is line-work, just below the threshold at which a shape commits to being a thing.
detail: Violet and gold only, with the gold threads passing over the violet, never the reverse.
The lower-left region is drawn with the same line weight as the rest — nothing about it announces itself except that it almost resolves.
Line-work density is lower than issue 23's throughout: this panel is prettier and emptier, and that is the difference.
neg: the suggested figure must never resolve — no face, no hands, no legs
no focal object, no ground plane, no horizon
do not make the filigree denser; lower density is correct here

math: Three rows of panels. Row 1: 4 panels. Row 2: 2 panels, the left one double-width. Row 3: 3 panels. Total 9 panels.
Outer margin 0.050 of frame width, gutters 0.030 horizontally and 0.026 vertically. Row heights: 0.280, 0.280, 0.280 of frame height.
Beat sequence, read left to right then top to bottom: whirl, hand, small figure, tunnel. Four beats across nine panels — the hand gets one panel, the whirl two, the figure one, the tunnel five.
Magenta accent covers 0.055 of the frame area in total, in three separate placements — never more than 0.025 in any one panel.
This is the only issue in the series that is already a finished comic PAGE rather than a cover.
detail: Cream paper, black ink, one magenta accent, exactly as the register requires.
Real brush inking: stroke weight follows form, and the screentone is a 45% dot over the shadow shapes only.
The four beats are drawn as four genuinely different images, not as one image repeated with variations.
neg: no word may be readable in any panel
no speech balloon
no page number, no corner box, no logo

math: The ground is INVERTED: cream-white paper at high luminance, magenta as the only ink. This is the only issue in the series on a pale ground.
Figure 0.10 of frame width by 0.17 high, centred at (50%, 78%), standing alone, seen from behind.

Eye-form: 0.20 of frame width by 0.09 high, centred at (50%, 36%) — deviation from the figure's own vertical axis is exactly 0. The symbol and the head share one axis, which is what makes the pair a single statement.
The empty gap between the eye's lower edge (y = 31.5%) and the figure's head (y = 69.5%) is 0.38 of frame height and is completely empty. The distance is the image.
detail: Figure in magenta ink only, a closed silhouette with a hood — no face, no hands.
Eye-form is a single almond in magenta line-work with a filled pupil, drawn at the same weight as the figure.
Because the ground is pale, the line-work frequency drops to 50% of the register's usual: the image is quieter than its siblings and must stay that way.
neg: no near-black anywhere — the ground stays pale
no second figure
nothing at all in the gap between eye and head
no text

math: 23 chevrons stacked vertically on a pitch of 0.037 of frame height, filling 23*0.037 = 0.851 of frame height. The column runs from y = 7.5% to y = 92.5%.
The column's axis is VERTICAL at x = 50%. Chevron width 0.10 of frame width, height 0.024, arms at 38 degrees above horizontal.
Every one of the 23 chevrons points EAST: tip at +x, tail at -x, arm angle -38 degrees on the upper edge and +38 on the lower. Zero exceptions across all 23.
This is the deliberate test of canon rule 1. The axis is vertical and every road segment still points east, so rule 1 is VISIBLE rather than violated.
detail: Chevrons are drawn as double strokes: a heavy inner stroke and a hairline outer, so the stack has weight without becoming solid.
Alternating chevrons carry a faint magenta and a faint cyan, so the column has a slow pulse without any of them changing direction.
The ground is near-black with engraved line-work at 20% frequency, so the column has something to be vertical against.
neg: all 23 chevrons must point east — not one may point north, west, or down
no vertical arrow
no text, no numerals in the column

math: Two outlined triangles on a common circumcircle of radius 0.30 centred at (50%, 50%): one upright with vertices at 90, 210 and 330 degrees; one inverted with vertices at 270, 30 and 150 degrees.
Six of the seven points therefore sit ON the circumcircle, at 30-degree intervals. They are correct and they are not the point of the image.

The SEVENTH point is the inverted triangle's lower vertex, displaced 0.070 of frame width EAST of its correct position at 270 degrees. It lands at 3 degrees off the circle — visibly, measurably wrong.
Every edge is a 0.006 of frame width outline. No fill on either triangle, no intersection shading, no double-line at the crossings.
detail: The seven points read at a glance because the first six are so correct that the eye assumes the seventh is too.
Outlines are engraved-weight and constant. The displaced vertex is drawn in exactly the same weight as the other six — the mistake is positional, never stylistic.
The ground is near-black with the faintest engraved line-work, so the frame is still and empty around the geometry.
neg: exactly seven points — the seventh must be off-axis by 0.070
no fill, no hatching inside either triangle
no text, no annotation of the geometry

math: STROKE BUDGET: 34 contour passes for the entire image. This is the fewest of all 48 covers and the sparsest line-work in the series. Do not add strokes to improve it.
Suit 0.36 of frame width by 0.52 of frame height, centred at (50%, 54%), shoulders at y = 32%, hem at y = 78%.
Hanger hook: a single arc of radius 0.03 at (50%, 16%), and the hook is drawn with ONE stroke. The hanger itself is 3 strokes.
The hood-shaped void where a head would be: 0.11 wide by 0.15 high at (50%, 30%), filled with the ground colour. Features inside it: ZERO — not eyes, not a shadow, not a suggestion.
detail: One confident contour per edge, no doubling, no interior lines except the two lapel strokes and the sleeve seams — 4 interior strokes total.
Lapels, collar and cuffs are indicated by the turn of the single contour, not by drawn lines. A draughtsman's economy.
The suit hangs with no body in it: the shoulders hold shape from the coat's structure alone, and the hem falls straight.
neg: do NOT add detail — the emptiness is the quality
the head void must have no features at all
no shading, no hatching, no second colour

math: The hood fills the frame: 0.62 of frame width by 0.74 of frame height, centred at (50%, 50%).
The hood is a SOLID MASS at luminance 0.01 across 0.46 of the frame area — the single largest dark shape in the series. No texture inside it, no hood opening, no interior.
Rim light: a single thin red line 0.008 of frame width wide, along the RIGHT contour only, covering 31% of that contour from y = 30% to y = 61%. The other 69% of the contour has no rim at all.
The rim is the ONLY saturated colour in the image and it occupies less than 1% of the frame area.
detail: One dominant shape, no secondary objects, no background incident — the hood is the whole image.
The red rim is a hairline of pure light with no glow and no bloom. A glow would soften the silhouette; the silhouette must stay absolute.
The ground outside the hood is near-black with engraved line-work at 15% frequency — present only so the hood's edge has something to cut against.
neg: no face, no hood opening, no neck, no hands
no second rim light on the left
no glow, no bloom on the rim

math: One eye, low in the frame: 0.30 of frame width by 0.17 of frame height, centred at (50%, 74%), looking down a corridor.
Corridor: two walls converging on a single vanishing point at (50%, 40%). Wall blue occupies 0.56 of the frame area.
Six lamps on the walls, alternating walls, on a depth pitch that compresses toward the vanishing point; each lamp 0.045 wide by 0.02 high and emitting to a radius of 0.11.
The green iris occupies 0.021 of the frame area and appears NOWHERE ELSE. It is the only third colour in the image and it is confined to the iris.
detail: Blue and orange is the strongest pair for power, so the corridor is built from them entirely: deep blue walls, orange lamp pools on the floor and the far wall.
The lamps are the only hard light sources and each casts a visible pool; the corridor between them falls to near-black.
The eye is large enough to hold the frame's attention at 200 px — its silhouette is a single almond and its iris a single circle.
neg: green must not appear on the walls, the floor, or the lamps
no second eye
no text

math: One ink only: crimson on cream paper. Second ink in the image: zero.
TONE SYSTEM: exactly 3 line weights (0.004, 0.008, 0.014 of frame width) and 4 dot densities (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%). That is 12 distinct tone values, and the image uses no others.
Road: 0.055 of frame width, entering the left edge at y = 62% and leaving the right edge at y = 62%. Slope exactly 0 — it runs east and it does not turn.
Figure: 0.09 of frame height, standing on the road at (50%, 56%), so it interrupts the road's horizontal without displacing it.
detail: The figure is 6 strokes and nothing more: hood outline, two shoulders, two legs, one ground contact. Its smallness is the argument.
All separation is by line weight and dot density: the road is a double weight, the horizon is a 25% dot field, the figure is solid.
Cream paper is warm and slightly textured; the crimson is a single flat ink with no shading and no second pass.
neg: no second ink, ever
no grey, no black, no additional hue
the road must stay horizontal
no more than 6 strokes on the figure

math: Pure geometry. Outer amber rectangle inset 0.070 of frame width on all four sides. One inner margin rule inset 0.110.
Four corner crop marks, each 0.060 long and 0.006 wide, offset 0.040 from the frame corner.
The interior of the inner rule is 0.78 x 0.78 = 0.6084 of the frame area and it is EMPTY: zero objects, zero marks, zero texture — not even paper grain beyond a flat tint.
Stroke budget: 2 rectangles (4 strokes) + 4 crop marks (8 strokes) = 12 strokes total. That is the whole image.
detail: Amber ink on cream paper, single ink, hairline weight — the skeleton and never the labelled version.
The rules are dead straight and dead parallel: the gap between outer rectangle and inner rule is 0.040 of frame width on all four sides, identical to within 0.002.
The paper's flat tint is the only texture. Any grain in the field is a failure of the brief.
neg: the field must be empty — generate the skeleton, never the labelled one
no crop marks inside the frame, none in the field
no text, no numbers, no registration marks

math: Measure 0.88 of frame width on all four margins, then a 12-column grid inside it: column width 0.0563, gutter 0.016, so 12*0.0563 + 11*0.016 = 0.676 + 0.176 = 0.852 — and the remaining 0.028 is the outer margin the grid does not reach.

Chrome, top to bottom: title band 0.090 of frame height at the top; year at 0.040 cap height in the top right; subtitle band 0.045 below the title; four section headers at 0.035 cap height, evenly distributed down the left column.

Blocks: topology diagram 0.52 wide by 0.30 high centred at (50%, 42%); legend 0.20 wide by 0.24 high at (26%, 76%); body copy block 0.44 wide by 0.16 high at (64%, 80%). No two blocks overlap by more than 0.004.

Real text: exactly AMPHETAMEMES in the title band, 2025 in the top right, SYSTEM ATLAS in the subtitle. Three strings, 28 characters (12 + 4 + 12). Everything else is word-SHAPED with the rhythm of language and no meaning.
detail: The whole infographic survives on layout alone: correct grid, correct hierarchy, correct spacing, correct alignment. Remove the words and it still reads as a real document.
The topology diagram is real — 3 clusters of 4 nodes with real connections, drawn in the register's hairline cyan.
The gibberish text has real letter rhythm, real word lengths (4 to 9 letters) and real baselines; only the letters themselves are wrong. It must never resolve into a readable word.
neg: only three real strings: AMPHETAMEMES, 2025, SYSTEM ATLAS
no other readable word or number anywhere, including the legend and the body copy
no lorem ipsum that a viewer could parse

math: Exactly 30 nodes in three classes of ten: 10 circles, 10 squares, 10 triangles, in three colours.
62 edges, giving a mean degree of 2*62/30 = 4.13 per node.

Force-simulation layout: mean nearest-neighbour distance 0.11 of frame width, and 3 node pairs sit closer than 0.05. A perfectly tidy layout does NOT read as generated — the small overlaps are the signature of the simulation.
Library name Chart.js in the lower right corner at cap height 0.026, right-aligned to the 0.94 margin. It is the only text in the image.
detail: Nodes are outlined shapes of uniform stroke weight; a few are filled at 20% to indicate class. Nothing is filled at 100%.
Edges are hairlines at 0.0025 of frame width, and 4 of them cross without a jump-over — the untidiness is the point.
Background: the register's faint concentric rings and thin grid, so the graph sits on the same ground as the rest of the series.
neg: Chart.js is the only text — no axis labels, no title, no tick numbers, no legend text
no more than 30 nodes
do not tidy the layout

math: Nine layers in cross-section, stacked vertically: each 0.072 of frame height with 0.012 gaps, so 9*0.072 + 8*0.012 = 0.648 + 0.096 = 0.744 of frame height. The stack runs from y = 12% to y = 86.4%.

Real text: LAYER 1 through LAYER 9, one per layer, 9 strings and 63 characters (9 x 7), at cap height 0.022, left-aligned at x = 10% and baseline-aligned to each layer's vertical centre. Nothing else in the frame is readable.
Rule weights: dimension rules 0.003 of frame width, leader lines 0.003, layer separators 0.005, frame border 0.008. No rule anywhere exceeds 0.008 — a heavier rule would break the drawing's grammar.
Dimension rules: 3 on the left, 2 on the bottom. Leader lines: 11, each landing on a layer boundary. Tick-marked scales in 0.012 increments along the bottom dimension rules.
Title block 0.26 wide by 0.16 high in the lower right, with 6 empty fields and no text in any of them.
detail: Blueprint grammar, drawn correctly: extension lines offset 0.010 from the object, arrowheads at 0.008, leaders at 30 degrees to horizontal, every rule thin, straight and parallel.
Cream-orange palette, cream sheet, orange rules, deep navy line — no wash, no shading, no tonal fill anywhere.
The layers are drawn as real cross-sections: hatch-free outlines with internal detail lines, each layer distinct from its neighbours.
neg: LAYER 1 to LAYER 9 is the only text, including inside the title block
no other dimension value, no scale number, no sheet number, no revision block text
no rule thicker than 0.008
no hand-drawn wobble on any straight rule

math: Nine figures of identical build, 0.11 of frame width by 0.30 of frame height each, at nine different stages of one gesture.
They are staggered along ONE diagonal from (14%, 86%) to (86%, 22%): step 0.09 east and 0.08 north per figure, so the diagonal's pitch = atan(0.08/0.09) = 41.6 degrees.
Adjacent centres are 0.1206 of frame width apart on that diagonal, which is just over one figure width — so figures overlap slightly without merging.
Occlusion budget: no single figure may be overlapped by more than 2 others. All 9 silhouettes must stay individually readable at 200 px.
detail: Nine stages of ONE gesture, so the arm angle advances monotonically while the body's weight shifts — a sequence, not nine poses.
Figures share one build and one palette, drawn as flat shapes with an outline; the palette entry is the only thing distinguishing them.
Depth is carried by value: figure 1 at full value, each subsequent figure 12% darker, so the diagonal reads front to back as well as left to right.
neg: no two figures may be in the same stage of the gesture
no more than 2 figures overlapped by any one
no ground line

math: Five slabs on a base. Slab widths taper 0.240, 0.216, 0.194, 0.175, 0.157 of frame width — each 0.9x the one below, a 1.53:1 fall from bottom to top.
Each slab is 0.100 of frame height, on a vertical pitch of 0.120, so the stack occupies 5*0.100 + 4*0.020 = 0.580 of frame height, from y = 24% to y = 82%.
Base: 0.28 of frame width by 0.06 high, top edge at y = 82%, centred at (50%, 85%).
The perched shape: 0.06 wide by 0.05 high at (50%, 19%), touching the top slab's upper edge exactly. It is a quarter of the top slab's width.
detail: Slabs are stone: an edge bevel catching light along the top and a shadow under each overhang, so the stack has five distinct planes.
The taper is the point — a vertical stack with something on top is a spine, and the narrowing sells the height.
No ground plane, no horizon, no cast shadow on a floor. The stack stands in the frame's void.
neg: no ground, no floor, no horizon
the slabs must taper — equal widths read as a wall
no figures, no faces on the slabs

math: Trunk 0.46 of frame width, running from the bottom edge (y = 100%) to y = 14% — 0.86 of frame height. It is cropped by the frame at the base and at the crown, so its full height is unknowable.
Bark fissures: irregular vertical channels 0.008 to 0.020 of frame width wide, running the full height, count approximately 34 across the trunk's width. Nothing else draws the bark.

The face is formed BY the fissures and is never drawn on top of them: 2 eyes 0.035 wide, centres at (44%, 42%) and (56%, 42%), spacing 0.12; mouth 0.09 wide centred at (50%, 55%). Each feature is a place where fissures PART, so the face is negative space.
Zero added lines for the face: the count of drawn strokes is the count of bark fissures and nothing more.
Halo at the crown: 24 gold rays at 15-degree intervals, each 0.070 of frame width long, radiating from a 0.12-radius centre at (50%, 10%).
detail: Bark as face plus a halo crown equals authority. The bark is drawn first and well; the face is what the eye finds afterwards.
The trunk is lit from the upper left at 35 degrees, so the fissures on the right run into shadow and the face's right side falls away — a calm face, not a symmetric mask.
The gold rays are thin flat strokes with no glow and no gradient; the halo is an engraving convention, not a light effect.
neg: no eyes, mouth or features drawn as separate marks — they must be the bark
no leaves, no branches, no canopy
no second face in the bark

math: Dead centre at (50%, 50%). Body 0.34 of frame width by 0.62 of frame height. This is the one cover in the series that is symmetrical and still, and it has to feel final.
Split axis at exactly x = 50.0%: left half cyan at 100% coverage, right half magenta-gold at 100%. Seam width 0, hard cut, no blend.
Crown of fire: 13 tongues, each 0.09 of frame width long, radiating 24 degrees apart from (50%, 19%), reaching y = 10%. Count them: 13.
Stillness budget: zero blur, zero motion lines, zero lean, zero gesture. Every edge in the image is either vertical, horizontal, or a 24-degree ray from the crown. Nothing else is permitted.
detail: The being is symmetrical because it is one being, not two: the split is a temperature division, so the two halves are the same drawing in different light.
Crowned in fire: the 13 tongues are engraved flame-structure with hard edges, magenta-gold on the right, cyan-flame on the left.
Symmetry holds to within 0. A viewer must be able to fold the image down the centre line and have it match, which is the test of whether the thesis landed.
The ground carries engraved line-work at 30% frequency and does nothing else — the being has the frame to itself.
neg: no motion of any kind — blur, lean, gesture, motion lines all forbidden
no text, no title
the two halves must match in shape, not only in size
